08/17.08.2023 This criminal revision has been preferred on behalf of petitioner
against the order dated 25.08.2022 passed by the learned District and Additional Sessions Judge-I,
Ghatshila, East Singhbhum whereby the petition of the petitioner under section 227 of Cr.PC has
been rejected in S.T Case No. 176 of 2021, arising out of Ghatshila P.S. Case No.26 of 2020.
2.  The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that from the allegations made in the FIR itself no alleged offence is made out against the petitioner.

The petitioner and the victim both were the major and the sexual relation established between them consensually and this FIR was lodged simply on account of breach of promise to marry and on this ground no alleged offence under section 376 of IPC is made out against the petitioner.

3. In support of his contention, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied para-16 and 17 of "Naim Ahamed v. State (NCT of Delhi)" 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 66.
4.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned APP on behalf of State opposed the contentions made by learned counsel for the petitioner and contended that the very intention of the petitioner since beginning was to obtain the consent of the victim having promised her to marry.
As such, the alleged offence against the petitioner is made out and the order passed by the learned court below needs no interference.
5. It is the settled law that while framing the charge, the Court has to go through the allegations made in the FIR and also the evidence collected by the IO during investigation.

sentences.text: 6. From the perusal of the FIR itself, it is found that the victim gave the written information with the police station concerned with these allegations that her love affair was going on for the last two and half years with Kanhu Murmu and who had been residing at the house of his maternal uncle.

She came in contact of him two and half years ago and weekly he used to call her to meet towards the canal and on the pretext of marriage, he had been establishing physical relation with her and he used to come to her house and asked to open the door otherwise he would be sitting there.

When she asked her in regard to getting married with her, he deviated from the same and he even had stopped talking to her and no where about was known of him, he is absconding from the house for the last four days.

On this written information, the case crime no. 0026 of 2020 was lodged with the Police Station Ghatshila, District Jamshedpur under section 376 of IPC.
7.
The statement of victim was recorded in para-3 of the case diary, in which, she corroborated the prosecution story.

In para-10 of the case diary, the witness Dukhu Ram Soren was interrogated, he is the father of victim and stated that the accused has been establishing physical relation with his daughter on the pretext of marriage since 2017.
In para-11 of the case diary, Sumit Mandal was interrogated that he belongs to the same caste of the victim and in regard to the affairs between the two, every one of the village was well aware.
He never made attempt to know in regard to the physical relation between them.
In view of para-16 of the case diary, the date of birth of victim is 12.4.1989.
The statement of victim was recorded under section 164 of Cr.PC which is given in para-35 of the case diary.

The victim has stated that after having given the promise to marry her, he had been establishing physical relation with her since 2017 and everything was going well; but in the year 2019 he was seen with another girl by her sister and, thereafter, he also fled away having enticed one Yasoda Mardi three or four days ago in April, 2020.
Para-49 of the case diary is the medical examination of the report of the victim, wherein it is opined that the old rupture hymen goes in favour of sexual intercourse.

8. The charge-sheet has been filed by the IO, wherein, from the allegation made in the FIR itself by the victim in her statement under section 164 of Cr.PC, she has stated that since very inception two and half years ago from the date of lodging FIR, the accused had been establishing physical relation with her on the pretext of marriage.

The love affairs developed between them on the very pretext of marriage, though, the victim and the accused both were the major, so far as the consent is concerned in view of section 90 of IPC, the consent was obtained under misconception making the false pretext of marriage with her and it was from the very inception, this promise was not given after establishing the physical relation.

In the case law, in "Naim Ahamed v. State (NCT of Delhi)"
(supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed in para-17 "Dr. Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar v. State of Maharashtra and others" (2019) 18 SCC 191 interpreting the section 90 and the Clause secondly in section 375 of IPC, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that there is a clear distinction between the mere breach of a promise and not fulfilling a false promise.

sentences.text: If the accused has not made the promise with the sole intention to seduce the prosecutrix to indulge in sexual acts, such an act would not amount to rape.

Where the prosecutrix agrees to have sexual intercourse on account of her love and passion for the accused and not solely on account of the misconception created by the accused, on account of the circumstances which he could not have foreseen or which were beyond his control,
was unable to marry despite having every intention to do so such case must be treated differently.
Mala fide intention if he had clandestine motives, it is a clear case of rape.

sentences.text:
consensual physical relationship between the parties would not constitute an offence under section 376 IPC.
9.
Herein case in hand, there is mala fide intention on the part of the accused as he on pretext of marriage established physical relation with her.
Subsequently, not only he refused to marry with her but he also came in contact with another girl as transpired from the statement of victim under section 164 of Cr.PC.
Herein there is nothing on the part of accused that on account of some grave or exceptional circumstances, he was not in a position to marry with her.
The consent which was obtained from the victim was under the pretext of marriage.
As such, the court below while rejecting the discharge application of the petitioner has committed no illegality, the impugned order passed by court below needs no interference.
10. Accordingly, this criminal revision petition is dismissed.
